column3: The Hebrew commands give glory; BSB expresses may the glory be to His name.
The Hebrew presents doing all He desired as completed; BSB says He does as He pleases.
The Hebrew has a singular human in the phrase hands of man; BSB says hands of men.
The Hebrew has a singular mouth and says they do not speak or see, without explicit ability verbs; BSB has mouths and cannot.
The Hebrew has a singular nose and states not hearing or smelling without explicit ability verbs; BSB has noses and cannot.
The Hebrew names making a sound in their throat; BSB says clearing their throats.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name us after the first blessing verb; BSB supplies us.
The Hebrew repeats you and names sons; BSB uses both and says children.
The Hebrew states they are blessed; BSB expresses a wish.
The Hebrew repeats heavens without an explicit highest; BSB says highest heavens and mankind instead of sons of man.
